correctness.rationale: I independently recomputed the distances by breadth-first search from every vertex of the explicit Cartesian-product graph, not by the supplied formula. A triple is excluded exactly when twice the maximum of its three distances equals their sum: concatenating geodesics for the two shorter distances then gives a shortest path containing the third vertex. Enumerating increasing faces by adding one vertex and testing all newly introduced triples is exhaustive by heredity. No face of size ≥5 survives. From the signed chain matrices I recomputed Smith forms over ℤ using SymPy 1.14.0; all nonzero factors have absolute value one. Thus im ∂_(i+1) is saturated in C_i, and H_i embeds into a free cokernel, so it is free. The complete 1-skeleton is connected. For n=3..8, the boundary ranks (r1,r2,r3) are (5,7,0),(7,6,2),(9,31,10),(11,31,18),(13,71,56),(15,73,72). The dimensions then give reduced Betti triples (3,1,0),(15,0,0),(5,9,0),(24,3,0),(7,27,0),(32,15,4), with no unlisted reduced homology. In particular H̃3 first occurs at n=8 with rank 76−72=4. Replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence/ladder_homology.py; results in ladder_homology.log in that directory. I inspected the supplied proof and unit-pivot implementation without running the supplied code. Verification is for n=3..8 only.

evidence: The Cartesian-product theorem already determines the general-position number 3 at n=3 and 4 at n≥4. The open-ladder result computes integral homology for all n≥2 on P_n × K2. Published stronger homotopy results on circular ladders concern independence or perfect-matching complexes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known cylinder family theorem fixes dimension and hence vanishing above degree 3, not the rank in degree 3 once tetrahedra occur. Adding cyclic edges to an open ladder changes metric betweenness; the all-order open-ladder or other-complex theorems do not specialize to this homology.

evidence: The published gp value is already 4 from n=4, but the verified H̃3 remains zero for n=4,5,6,7. Face counts would determine Euler characteristic but not ranks of both ∂2 and ∂3 or torsion. The three-cut theorem gives a sphere-wedge for a different forbidden-triple system.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the known dimension calculation, which determines where H̃3 could possibly occur, but not where it first does occur. Neither those counts nor the inspected dual result yield the Smith-form census by specialization.

evidence: The target is the independence complex of the forbidden geodesic-triple hypergraph, not the graph independence complex. The Resultary three-cut record uses complements of disconnected induced triples; its dual instead avoids disconnected triples.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The three consecutive vertices of a layer for n≥5 form a connected induced path and a forbidden geodesic triple, so the two triple rules differ on the same graph. Matching complexes use edges, not the target vertex sets. The inspected cut dual on C4 × Cn additionally uses a different graph. No equivalence is supplied by these formulations.

value.rationale: For this canonical family of known general-position dimension, the first top-dimensional cycle is not where tetrahedra first exist. The sharp onset and torsion-free full profiles distinguish that phenomenon from the already-known extremal size, and give exact tests for any proposed cyclic-ladder homotopy or chain model. The finite end point is dictated by the first occurrence, not an arbitrary truncation. No homotopy-type classification or result beyond the cutoff is inferred.
